name_reason: Name already compliant. Prefix data_fd2_battle_ is correct (battle-core data table). Descriptor 'spell_learning_table' accurately reflects both the purpose (per-class spell-learn schedule) and the data type (table/array). No Ghidra address residue; no domain-ID component to preserve or strip. Reflects the array datatype via the '_table' suffix.
purpose: Read-only per-class spell-learning schedule table: maps a character growth class to the (level -> spell_id) pairs that the character learns as it levels up.
logic_summary: 240-byte read-only const region (.object3) at 0x626B3 = 20 entries x 12-byte stride. Indexed by the bSpell_learning_idx field of a character's growth entry (data_fd2_battle_character_growth_table[*]+0xA; 0xFF = learns no spells), NOT by portrait id. Each 12-byte entry is 6 (level, spell_id) byte pairs; 0xFF level marks an unused pair slot. Sole accessor fd2_get_spell_learning_entry @ 0x4E4AF returns &table[idx] (= 0x626B3 + idx*0xC). Sole indirect consumer fd2_process_xp_and_level_up_for_char @ 0x1E292: after each level-up, walks the 6 pairs reading *(byte*)(base + i*2)=req_level and *(byte*)(base + i*2 + 1)=spell_id; when req_level == the character's new level, grants that spell (fd2_grant_spell_to_char) and shows the learn dialog. Members are read as bytes (flat uint8 layout, columns alternate level/spell_id).
datatype: const uint8[20*12] in src (flat byte view); Ghidra datatype is spell_learning_entry[20] (240 bytes). Both describe the same 240-byte read-only region; the flat-uint8 src form matches the byte-by-byte access in the consumer. Datatype/dimension not in scope for this stage.
element_semantics: Logical layout = 20 entries x (6 x {uint8 level, uint8 spell_id}). Per entry, up to 6 ascending (level, spell_id) pairs; level = the character level at which the spell is learned (level-space, e.g. 1..30/40/99), spell_id = FD2 spell id in 0x00..0x23 space (verified against the canonical spell list, e.g. 0x11=魔刃術, 0x01=烈炎術, 0x1A=毒擊術, 0x02=炎龍術, 0x1B=麻痹術). A pair with level byte 0xFF (and spell byte 0xFF) is an empty/unused slot. Data is byte-identical to FD2.LE .object3 @ 0x626B3.
notes: is_const=true: only one xref to the address (the accessor at 0x4E4AF, DATA read); no writer anywhere; data byte-identical to binary -> true read-only -> correct as const. Verified data values byte-for-byte against read_memory (first row 05 11 09 01 0F 1A 15 02 1A 1B FF FF and last row 02 22 06 23 0B 17 0F 03 13 21 17 20 both match the C initializer). src comment block (btltab3.c lines 883-896) is already a precise, correct, ASCII-only conclusion (size/stride/index-semantics/pair-layout/0xFF-empty/byte-access) -> kept. Ghidra side: the detailed data documentation lives in the PRE_COMMENT (PLATE_COMMENT is null); its content is consistent with the refined understanding and the spell-name annotations all verify correct against the canonical spell list -> not contradictory/outdated/blank -> left unchanged per 'consistent => do not touch plate' rule (no content-driven reason to migrate PRE->PLATE in this narrow refine stage).
